narrative_purpose: Shows why the everyday animal bond is cheap enough to work: the rider sends one narrow high-level intention, while the banshee's own nervous system expands it locally into thousands of coordinated wing-muscle commands.
subject: A Na'vi rider bonded to a flying banshee in profile. Between the rider's queue and the animal's neural antenna runs one single thin luminous pulse. Inside the banshee, revealed in a transparent anatomical cutaway, that one pulse reaches a compact neural hub and fans outward into hundreds of fine branching paths distributed through both wings, chest, tail, and flight muscles; the enormous branching happens entirely inside the animal after the narrow link.
scene: A dark open-sky flight study combining the external bond with a clear internal cutaway of the mount's nervous and muscular branching.
camera: Broad side profile of rider and airborne animal, close enough to see the thin join and the internal fan of signals.
light: A bright but very narrow cyan thread marks the tsaheylu command; a much broader living-teal fan illuminates the animal's internal control paths.
palette: Cool night tones with cyan on the compact transmitted intent and teal across the locally expanded muscle-control web.
style: Painterly speculative-anatomy naturalist plate, one organism observed in motion with a restrained cutaway.
detail_level: Crisp at the queue join and neural hub, finely branched through the wings; the open sky remains soft and empty.
composition: Rider and bond occupy the upper-left, the banshee spans the frame, and the internal branching fan opens across the right two-thirds with dark sky around it.
consistency_notes: The transmitted path must remain one thin line until it reaches the banshee; only then may it explode into many local branches. Keep a plausible Pandoran flying body plan.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no reins, no cybernetic hardware, no Earth eagle, no photographic or 3D-render look, no neon UI, no gore
